description.narrative: The development objective of the Modernization of Public Finance Management (PFM) Project for Myanmar is to support efficient, accountable, and responsive delivery of public services through the modernization of Myanmar's PFM systems and strengthening institutional capacity. The project has five components. The first component will support developing systems and procedures for capturing more revenues from natural resource sectors on-budget and addressing identified weaknesses in tax administration. This component will be closely linked to government implementation of the extractive industries transparency initiative and will support the development of the business processes and corresponding reporting and recording systems to move revenues on-budget. The second component is aimed at supporting the new mandates of the budget and planning departments and the evolving decentralization process in Myanmar. To help inform decisions and debate on budgetary allocations, this component will also work towards improving the quality and timeliness of information available both internally and externally through basic computerization of current manual compilation process for the current and investment budgets. The third component, support for effective budget execution will focus on the establishment and effective operationalization of the treasury department, creating an effective procurement function, and building the ability of Myanmar Economic Bank (MEB) to manage the state fund account in order to ensure business continuity in view of the Central Bank of Myanmar (CBM) separation from the Ministry of Finance (MOF). The fourth component will strengthen Myanmar's nascent structures for external oversight and accountability and thus complement improvements in the quality and transparency of budgetary information. It has following two sub-components: (i) supporting the parliamentary public accounts committee; and (ii) enhancing operational effectiveness of the auditor general's office. The fifth component aims to address the specific challenges faced by Myanmar with respect to the skills required to operate a modern public financial management system. The project will support the establishment of a PFM academy that will serve as a nucleus for developing and facilitating provision of just in time, on the job, operational training within a sustainable framework.

The development objective of the project is to support efficient, accountable and responsive delivery of public services through the modernization of Myanmar's PFM systems and strengthening institutional capacity.

Finance Agreement :Project Operations Manual | Description :The Recipient shall ensure that the Project is carried out inaccordance with the arrangements and procedures set out in the Project Operations Manual. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

title.narrative: Timeliness of reconciled budget execution reports

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved the end target of >/=3. Treasury completed the Monthly Union Fund account within two months of the following the accounting month and submitted it to MoPFI, OAG, and Cabinet.</p>

title.narrative: Number of beneficiaries of training courses

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved the end target of 300. 1,428 staff are benefited through the PFM Academy as of 31st March 2021.</p>

title.narrative: Improving information base for linking budgets to plans- number of departments submitting recurrent and capital budget forms electronically

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved end target of 40. All 181 agencies submitted recurrent and capital budget forms electronically for the FY2019/20 budget.</p>

title.narrative: Number of large and medium tax-payers completing self-assessment

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved the end target of 2,300. A total of 7,637 (952 large taxpayers and 6,685 medium taxpayers) have been serviced by the self-assessment system from October 2020 to March 2021.</p>

title.narrative: Number of key budget and fiscal documents published on the MoPF website for public access

target.value: The end of project target for number of key fiscal documents publicly available has been increased to 9, including a budget dashboard and a report on gender informed budgeting for 1 service sector.

comment.narrative:
<p>Achieved. The public can access the 9 key fiscal documents at https://www.mopf.gov.mm. Citizen’s Budget (FY2020/21) and gender-informed budgeting in Social Sector report published in November 2020.</p>
<p> </p>

actual.value: The public can access the following 7 documents at https://www.mopf.gov.mm 1. 2019/20FY Annual budget law 2. Budget summary (pre-budget statement) 3. Budget Speech 4. Citizens Budgets 5. Annual budget report 6. Mid-year budget report 7. Quarterly budget report 8.2019/20FY Budget Estimate GFS 9. 2019/20FY Fiscal Policy. The budget dashboard is not operational. title.narrative: Composition of expenditure out-turn compared to original approved.

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved the final target of 14. The composition of expenditure (temporary actual) out-turn variance compared to the original approved FY2019/20 was -0.36%</p>

title.narrative: New Financial Rules and Regulations are enaced and published

baseline.value: Financial rules and regulations outdated and not widely available.

target.value: Updated financial rules and regulations published and adopted.

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. Updated and published Financial Rules and Regulations in 2017. The official English version of the financial rules and regulations (FRR) was approved and posted on the MOPF website in October 2018.</p>

actual.value: Official English version of the financial rules and regulations (FRR) approved and posted on MOPF website in October 2018.

title.narrative: Budget preparation process including (i) issuance of ceilings (ii) preparation of medium-term fiscal framework

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. Budget Department issued the budget ceiling to line ministries and prepared the medium-term fiscal framework since FY2015/16.</p>

title.narrative: Timeliness of Submission of Audit Report to Parliament

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved <12 months although end target was <10 months due to the COVID-19 situation. The Audit Report for FY 2018/19 was submitted to Parliament on 4th Sept 2020 and within 12 months.</p>

title.narrative: Increase in Tax collection from Large Taxpayers

baseline.value: Baseline: Taxes collected by LTO in FY 2015-2016 was 1,105,670 million MMK.

target.value: Taxes collected by LTO for FY 2020/21 is estimated at 3,250,000 million MMK

comment.narrative:
<p>The initial indicator measuring the Tax to GDP ratio goes well beyond the project scope and revised the indicator in the 2019 restructuring paper with an Increase in Tax collection from Large Taxpayers. Since the project was directly supporting the Large taxpayers' office and increased enforcement through the international tax audit advisers.</p>
<p>Achieved the end target of MMK 3,250,000 million MMK. Since taxes collected by LTO in FY 2019/20 (as of 8th Sept 2020) stood at 3,665,156 million MMK, the first half of FY 2020/21 (October 2020 to March 2021) stood at 1,097,423 million MMK. </p>

actual.value: Taxes collected by LTO from large taxpayers in FY 2019/20 (as of 8th Sept 2020) stood at 3,665,156 million MMK.

title.narrative: Information on procurement opportunities and contract awards (above USD 100 000) are publicly available for 5 Union ministries.

baseline.value: IPSAS standards are not applied in Myanmar accounting and financial reporting

target.value: MOPF and OAG have adopted a transition plan for the adoption of IPSAS over the medium term

comment.narrative:
<p>Achieved. This was a new result indicator. OAG and MoPFI adopted the IPSAS transaction plan in November 2019. To implement the IPSAS transition plan and road map, IPSAS preparatory committee was established in March 2020 and organized the quarterly meetings.</p>
<p>245 staff (from OAG, MoPFI and MoE) benefited from IPSAS Cash Basic training from 7th June to 2nd August 2020, and  217 staff (from OAG, MoPFI and MoE) benefited from IPSAS Accrual Basic training from 9th August to 27th December 2020 by support by EU.    </p>

actual.value: The IPSAS transition plan was jointly adopted by OAG and MOPF as of 30 November 2019

title.narrative: Capacity building of JPAC to Strengthen Parliamentary oversight

baseline.value: JPAC received initial capacity building notably on English and ICT skills as well as IT modernization. There is a need to strengthen JPAC's involvement in the drafting of the new PFM bill.

target.value: Publication of the draft PFM bill with inputs from JPAC

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. JPAC provided the inputs to the draft PFM Bill which was under review by Parliament.</p>

actual.value: JPAC provided the inputs to the draft PFM Bill

title.narrative: Delivery of a core banking system (CBS)

baseline.value: No such modern system existed. MEB treasury processes remain largely paper based.

target.value: The CBS is expected to be acquired and tested in Head office and a large branch in Yangon.

comment.narrative: <p>This is a new indicator in the 2019 restructuring paper. CBS contract was finalized by MEB and the successful bidder. WB and Government approved the CBS contract. However, given the current situation in Myanmar, the signing stage of CBS was on hold according to the applicable policies (OP/BP 7.30). The policy will guide the task team in determining further steps relative to the program. </p>

actual.value: The signing stage of Core Banking System contract

title.narrative: Establishement of the PFM training academy to enhance sustainability of PFM training

baseline.value: PFM academy is not yet operational

target.value: PFM academy is established and carrying out initial training. A gender disaggregated training monitoring and evaluation framework is operational.

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. PFM Academy was launched in February 2020 and delivered face-to-face training and created online training to government officials from all line ministries as well as the state and regional levels regarding 4 PFM modules as per PFM Acadmy Curriculum and other technical pieces of training by support from Development Partners. The standard operating procedure for PFM Academy was developed for the training program.  </p>

actual.value: Established PFM academy in February 2020 and carried out initial trainings and a refresher gender responsive budgeting trainings

baseline.value: The financial reporting is largely manual, cumbersome and prone to errors and delays.

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved the end target of 20. Treasury Automation (FIRST) was developed and implemented at pilot 20 agencies in 2020. FIRST training has been delivered by Treasury to 168 agencies in January 2021 for implementation.   </p>
